assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Accepting the legacy path as delivery again makes _delivered_review_record return the predecessor round and promote_review_run_itself refuse nothing, so the None assertion at 217 and promoted-is-false at 220 redden; gate-base-arm.log shows exactly this.
Dropping the same_revision, review_run_id or dispatch-time check lets the mismatched record at the head-keyed path deliver, so that case's None assertion reddens.
Removing the no-head refusal at recovery_review_acceptance.py:320 makes promote_review_run_itself promote on the legacy round, so the promoted-is-false and reason assertions redden.

assertion_independence: Each added assertion is the code under test's own return value against a fixture the test did not hand that function: the None assertions read _delivered_review_record's output, and the promotion assertions read the ledger row and refusal reason the production sweep produced. No added assertion compares a value against the same variable the test passed in.

findings.text: follow-on: _is_run_review_node answers 'is this a run review' only when the node id carries REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX, so in promote_review_run_itself (reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:320) the refusal that names the missing head is reached only for a review-prefixed node id; a run review hand-launched under a coordinator's own node id — a case recovery_review_delivery.py:57 and recovery_review_dispatch.py:150 both document as real — declares only a legacy path and is refused by the generic 'stored no readable record' branch instead of one naming the head. The refusal is still fail-closed, so this is a message-fidelity gap, not a delivery hole: _delivered_review_record returns None for any record that is not at a declared head-keyed path, so such a review cannot be promoted on another round's verdict.
